hypotheses.text: In the index SPAX11 kindreds carrying TUBA4A p.Glu415Lys (12 affected individuals across two families), dysarthria is present in only an intermediate subset (<50%) of affected individuals, whereas oculomotor abnormalities (nystagmus and broken smooth pursuit) show higher penetrance (>70%) among clinically evaluated patients.
hypotheses.rationale: Discovery descriptions of the TUBA4A p.Glu415Lys cohort explicitly qualify dysarthria as appearing 'sometimes', while highlighting oculomotor signs such as nystagmus and broken smooth pursuit alongside gait and spasticity. Defining exact cohort frequencies establishes whether speech impairment is an obligate or dispensable diagnostic criterion for SPAX11.

evidence.text: Torella et al. reported two families with spastic ataxia carrying the p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A (one with 11 affected individuals and another with a single patient), noting clinical findings including ocular movements (nystagmus, broken smooth pursuit) and 'sometimes dysarthria'.

source.title: A new genetic cause of spastic ataxia: the p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A
source.quote: ocular movements (nystagmus, broken smooth pursuit), and sometimes dysarthria.

hypotheses.text: Peripheral neuropathy in SPAX11 is an axonal sensory-motor neuropathy that manifests in adult life rather than early childhood, occurring in a minority of affected individuals with TUBA4A variants.
hypotheses.rationale: In the discovery report, peripheral nerve conduction studies performed at age 40 revealed an axonal sensory-motor neuropathy with electromyographic signs of denervation. Determining whether this feature is universal across adult family members or restricted to later-stage/older individuals will clarify whether normal nerve conduction studies exclude SPAX11.

evidence.text: In the report of TUBA4A p.Glu415Lys, peripheral nerve conduction studies (PNCS) performed at 40 years demonstrated axonal sensory-motor neuropathy and electromyography (EMG) signs of denervation in the examined proband.

source.title: A new genetic cause of spastic ataxia: the p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A
source.quote: PNCS, performed at 40 years, showed an axonal sensory-motor neuropathy and EMG signs of … ocular movements (nystagmus, broken smooth pursuit), and sometimes dysarthria.

evidence.text: A Tuba4a Q176P mouse model of SPAX11 exhibits overt ataxia and Purkinje neuron degeneration without motor neuron degeneration, corroborating that primary tubulin-mediated neurodegeneration in SPAX11 targets cerebellar networks while sparing primary motor neuron perikarya.

source.title: A mouse model of autosomal dominant spastic ataxia and myopathy caused by a mutation in Tuba4a
source.quote: Our mice exhibit hallmark features of SPAX11 and CMYO26, but do not show motor neuron degeneration.

hypotheses.text: The combination of broken smooth pursuit and nystagmus with lower limb spasticity differentiates SPAX11 from pure hereditary spastic paraplegias (such as SPG4), but fails to reliably distinguish it from AFG3L2-related spastic ataxia (SPAX5/SCA28) and TUBB4A-related disorders without genetic confirmation.
hypotheses.rationale: Both AFG3L2-associated disorders (SCA28/SPAX5) and TUBB4A-related disorders frequently present with cerebellar eye movement disorders (nystagmus, broken pursuit), dysarthria, and spasticity, mimicking the TUBA4A p.Glu415Lys clinical picture.

evidence.text: SCA28 caused by AFG3L2 pathogenic variants features young-adult onset gait/limb ataxia, cerebellar dysarthria, cerebellar and supranuclear eye movement disorders (including ptosis and ophthalmoplegia), and spasticity/pyramidal syndrome in individuals with longer disease duration.

source.title: AFG3L2-Related Neurologic Disorders
source.quote: Less frequently, ptosis/ophthalmoplegia, dysarthria, or upper-limb incoordination may occur as the initial finding. Pyramidal syndrome (increased and brisk reflexes, extensor plantar reflex, and spasticity) is commonly observed in individuals with longer disease duration.

evidence.text: TUBB4A-related neurologic disorders show progressive involvement of pyramidal tracts, extrapyramidal structures, cerebellum (ataxia, intention tremor, dysmetria), bulbar function (dysarthria, dysphonia), and ocular motor deficits including nystagmus.

source.title: TUBB4A-Related Neurologic Disorders
source.quote: Dysarthria and dysphonia require speech therapy and possible augmentative and alternative … of nystagmus, upper motor neuron dysfunction, gait ataxia, & extrapyramidal signs

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact patient-by-patient clinical and electrophysiological tables in Torella et al. (2023) detailing the presence or absence of peripheral neuropathy, dysarthria, and nystagmus across all 12 reported individuals?
new_directions.rationale: Directly extracting the individual-level numerator and denominator data will establish baseline statistical frequencies of these signs in SPAX11.

new_directions.question_text: Have subsequent independent clinical cohorts or single-case reports identified additional TUBA4A missense variants presenting with spastic ataxia, and what were the frequencies of sensory-motor neuropathy and dysarthria in those cases?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether p.Glu415Lys is unique or if other TUBA4A variants replicate the identical tri-feature phenotype (ataxia, spasticity, axonal neuropathy) is essential for generalizing the diagnostic algorithm.
